S.FORM: Mok suusuu pule maraw ēn qētēg m̄ērē heg.
S.TRANSL: Here is how my story begins.

S.FORM: Suusuu pule maraw heg avan moomä king avan m̄o, hahan i Qat.
S.TRANSL: This is the story of our former King, called Kpwat.

S.FORM: Älähä nē 'n tasun̄ mon too qatuu [ak]. 🌿
S.TRANSL: The story of how he carved himself a huge canoe. 🌿

S.FORM: On too qēn̄, Qat ēn van hag, tē tärä tul too qatuu qētē nanaa, sa ga [mäkä ak] mē.
S.TRANSL: One day, Kpwat went to the bush, and chopped down a large rosewood tree (Pterocarpus indicus) to make himself a canoe.

S.FORM: Nē 'n tärä va–van, nē 'n sēv, on rävräv nē tē mulä.
S.TRANSL: He chopped at it until it fell down; then evening came, and he returned back home.

S.FORM: Nē 'n n̄oo, on matpäh, nē 'n van tägäh hag: nanaa nen̄ ēn tuu ajew lēh nok.
S.TRANSL: He went to sleep, and on the next day, went back to the bush – but the tree was standing there again!

S.FORM: Nē tē tärä lēh.
S.TRANSL: So he started to chop it again.

S.FORM: Tärä tärä tärä va–van, nē 'n sēv, nē tē mulä.
S.TRANSL: He chopped it on and on and on until it fell; then he went back home.

S.FORM: Van, n̄oo, on matpäh nē 'n van ajew tägäh lēh hag: nanaa ēn tuu ajew lēh nok.
S.TRANSL: After a night at home, on the morning he walked back up to the bush – but the tree was standing up there once again!

S.FORM: Nē tē tärä lēh. Vag-tēl gēn ek.
S.TRANSL: So he went on to cut it down again. That was now the third time!

S.FORM: Tärä tärä va–van, nē 'n sēv, nē tē mulä.
S.TRANSL: He chopped it down, felled it, and went back home.

S.FORM: On matpäh nē 'n row tägäh hag, nanaa ēn tuu ajew lēh nok.
S.TRANSL: On the next morning he dashed back up to the bush, and saw the tree standing there once again.

S.FORM: Alē, nē sa “Ta! Noknok heg, na ga 'ēv woo to have heg, na ga ätä tuwoo sē gēn tē vaavaatuu lōk lēh nanaa na ok ēn tärä sēv!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: “Alright!” he thought, “This time, I’m going to hide somewhere here, and watch to figure out who has been standing back up that tree I keep trying to chop down!” 🌿

S.FORM: Nē 'n 'ēv, nē 'n 'ätä woo we i Wēmarawraw tē ät ma. Too vuu, hahan i Wēmarawraw.
S.TRANSL: So off he went to hide, and as he watched out, suddenly Butterfly appeared. It was a god, called Butterfly.

S.FORM: Nē 'n 'ēv, nē 'n petn̄äg too m̄asgi nanaa nē ok ēn tärä sēv [ak], tē petn̄äg too m̄asgi, tē 'ēv mē.
S.TRANSL: So Kpwat was hiding, holding a piece of wood from the tree he had been chopping down into a canoe: he had taken away that piece and gone into hiding.

S.FORM: Wēmarawraw nen̄ ēn row ma, ēn pahav lōk lēh ēn qētqētē nanaa nen̄ va–van,
S.TRANSL: As soon as he had landed in, Butterfly began to assemble back together the trunk of the rosewood tree.

S.FORM: nē tē tuu ajew lōk lēh, nē tē äm too m̄asgi gēn nen̄ Qat ok ēn petn̄äg.
S.TRANSL: He stood it up again, and started looking for that last piece Kpwat had hidden away.

S.FORM: Nē gēn tē äm gēn ek!
S.TRANSL: There he was now, searching everywhere!

S.FORM: Äm, ēn äm, ēn äm va–van, nē tē vaavuh sa “Ēy! Sē wōn have heg ēn petn̄äg too m̄asgi nanaa heg, nē a siivä mun na!”
S.TRANSL: Butterfly searched on and on: “Hey!” he exclaimed “Whoever hid a piece of this tree somewhere, I wish they brought it back to me!”

S.FORM: We Qat tē haläqäg jen le gawon.
S.TRANSL: And suddenly Kpwat leapt out from the bushes.

S.FORM: Haläqäg ma mēn mon tälä, sa “A, nēk gēn nen̄, nēk ok tē vaavaatuu lōk lēh nanaa na ok ēn tē tärä sēv? Na gēn a vuh nēk noknok heg le!”
S.TRANSL: “Ha ha!” he exclaimed, brandishing his axe, “So that was you! You were the one who kept standing back this rosewood tree every time I chopped it down? I’m killing you right now!”

S.FORM: Alē, Wēmarawraw sa “Ta, nēk mētē vuh lee na! Na a pirin̄ nēk. Wōjō a tärä lōk lēh ēn ak nen̄.”
S.TRANSL: “Mercy! Don’t kill me!” cried Butterfly, “I will help you. You and I will start your canoe again!”

S.FORM: Wōrō tē tärä lōk lēh.
S.TRANSL: So they resumed their work again.

S.FORM: Tärä va–van, ēn sēv, †wōrō tē wok /† wōrō tē tasun̄.
S.TRANSL: They chopped the tree down, and began to carve it.

S.FORM: Tasun̄ va–van ēn pah, wōrō tē vivih, tē ruruh to lē naw. 🌿
S.TRANSL: When they finished carving the canoe, they tied the pieces together, and finally dragged the canoe down to the sea. 🌿

S.FORM: We Qat tē van tē vis mun tuutuan. Tuutuan nen̄ [gaprä tuwa jēm̄ēn tuwa].
S.TRANSL: Then Kpwat went back to his brothers. He had eleven of them.

S.FORM: Van, vis mun gēē sa “Ōh! Mok qatuu ak nok ēhē! Noknok heg, gēj a maēs a van have, gēj a van ēs gēn ek.”
S.TRANSL: “Brothers!” he told them, “I now own an immense canoe! From now on, we’ll be able to go wherever we like!”

S.FORM: We wēē tuutuan nen̄ ēn ron̄ we gēē tē gäl nē.
S.TRANSL: As they heard him, his brothers decided to trick him.

S.FORM: Sa “Gēj a van vēgēn gangēj qawōō?”
S.TRANSL: “Let’s go pick up some almonds, shall we?” they proposed.

S.FORM: Gēē tē van hag lē qētē qawōō nen̄, sa “Sē gēn a vēgēn gēn ek?”
S.TRANSL: Once they had walked all the way up to the canarium trees, Kpwat asked “Alright, so who’s climbing first?”

S.FORM: Gēē sa “Nēk! Nēk a vēgēn!”
S.TRANSL: “You!” they replied, “You climb first!”

S.FORM: We Qat tē vēgēn.
S.TRANSL: So Kpwat climbed the tree.

S.FORM: Nē 'n vēgēn jēn̄ to hag nen̄, we an̄ä nen̄ tē rēg / qētē qawōō nen̄ tē rēg.
S.TRANSL: But as he reached the top of the tree, suddenly the canarium tree began to swell up!

S.FORM: Too sē jen gēē ēn mänäg qētē qawōō nen̄, qētē qawōō tē rēg, Qat ga hēw ēs avōh.
S.TRANSL: One of the brothers had cast a spell on the tree so it would swell up, and make Kpwat unable to come back down.

S.FORM: Alē, gēē tē van, gēē tē toto jen nē nē tē hag make [qawōō]. 🌿
S.TRANSL: Suddenly they took off and ran away from him, while he remained stuck on top of that tree. 🌿

S.FORM: Gēē 'n van, ruruh mon [ak], gēē tē [sō].
S.TRANSL: They rushed to find his canoe, dragged it out to the sea and began paddling.

S.FORM: Gēē tē sō jen [Vanōlav], gēē a maēs sa gēē a sō to [Lakon].
S.TRANSL: They were paddling away from Vanua Lava, aiming to reach Gaua.

S.FORM: Qat tē hag maken va–– van, nē 'n 'ätä woo we taqa tē kakal ma.
S.TRANSL: As for Kpwat, he was still sitting on top of the tree, when he suddenly saw a spider coming to him.

S.FORM: Taqa ēn kakal ma, sa / nē sala “Ey! Tuak! Nēk ga pirin̄ ēs na?”
S.TRANSL: As the spider came close, he said “Hey, my friend! Can you help me out?”

S.FORM: Taqa sa “Ga wē, na ga pirin̄ ēs nēk.”
S.TRANSL: – “Yes, said the spider, I can help you.”

S.FORM: Alē, nē tē mäkä 'n tien jen make än̄ä / qawōō, tē row jēn̄ hōw lē tanē, lōk lēh hag, nē 'n mäkä m̄ērē nen̄ va–van –
S.TRANSL: So it started to spin its silk from the top of the almond tree, slid all the way down to the ground, then back up, on and on and on —

S.FORM: nē 'n lekteg kere haj on Qat ga vēgēn suusuu / a hēw suusuu, alē Qat tē hēw suusuu ēn tie taqa nen̄.
S.TRANSL: when the web became solid enough for Kpwat to clamber along, he followed the spider’s silk all the way to the ground.

S.FORM: Jēn̄ hōw, ginteg tägäh hōw lē naw: mon ak gaiv nok!
S.TRANSL: As soon as he touched down, he rushed towards the shore, and realised his canoe had disappeared!

S.FORM: Tuutuan ēn pal nok, mēn mon gamtō, mēn gamtō mon Qat gēē tē to mē!
S.TRANSL: His brothers had stolen it, and run away with his wife, Kpwat’s wife!

S.FORM: Sa gēē a van mē [Lakon]. 🌿
S.TRANSL: They were on their way to Gaua. 🌿

S.FORM: We nē tē lä 'n too [vinlah], nē tē row ol lolon, mēn ōjēn vätäl ga men, nē tē hälä suusuu gēē.
S.TRANSL: Without further ado, Kpwat seized a coconut, and jumped inside. He had taken a supply of sweet bananas, and began to drift on the sea behind them.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n sō va– van, lē sēnē naw, gēē 'n 'ätä woo we, vinlah nen̄ tē hälä ma.
S.TRANSL: As for them, they were travelling on their canoe, in the middle of the ocean, when suddenly they took sight of a coconut that was drifting towards them.

S.FORM: Hälä hälä van ma, rigtäg we nē tē gän too vätäl ga men, tē 'äqä 'n vinn̄i.
S.TRANSL: As it was drifting closer and closer, Kpwat ate one of his sweet bananas, and threw the skin away.

S.FORM: Vinn̄i nē 'n hälä m̄o, tē 'äqä 'n vinn̄i, vinn̄i tē hälä ma.
S.TRANSL: The banana skin he tossed away also began to drift towards the canoe.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n van, 'ätä “Ey! Sē 'n gän vätäl ga men heg?”
S.TRANSL: As soon as they saw it, they said “Hey! Who just ate this sweet banana?”

S.FORM: Gēē a ron̄ avōh sa i Qat (va) la, Qat va nok lē [vinlah].
S.TRANSL: They had no idea this was really Kpwat, Kpwat who was hiding in the coconut.

S.FORM: Hag va–van, gēē tē ätä vērēgēl avōh, nē 'n gän lēh too vätäl tē äqä lēh.
S.TRANSL: So on they went, still bemused of what was happening. Then he ate a second banana, and threw the skin away again.

S.FORM: Gēē tē ätä vērēgēl vata avōh ni.
S.TRANSL: Still, they did not understand who that was.

S.FORM: Nē tē hälä m̄o. Van, jēn̄ to [Lakon] –
S.TRANSL: On and on they drifted, until they were in sight of Gaua.

S.FORM: Nē 'n hälä hag m̄ērē nen̄ we, gēē tē [sō] rigtäg nē päh, gēē tē lä 'n vinlah nen̄. Lä hōw lē ak, gēē tē van.
S.TRANSL: As he was still drifting like this, they pulled their canoe closer, and seized the coconut. They took it in their canoe, and went on.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n gih tē m̄ērē heg we nē tē wisis!
S.TRANSL: As they were holding it in their hands, Kpwat inside suddenly broke wind!

S.FORM: Puni tē ah we gēē tē äqä wutä nē.
S.TRANSL: The smell made them toss the coconut away.

S.FORM: We gēē tē sō va–van, jēn̄ [ma Lakon].
S.TRANSL: So on they went, closer and closer till they reached our island of Gaua.

S.FORM: [Qat nē 'n jēn̄ m̄o nok salēn, nē tē vēgēn make vaj tē hag jērē gēē. Gēē 'n sō ma, jēn̄ lē en, nē 'n häläqäg sēwēl tē saqal worä mon ak mēn mon tälä.]
S.TRANSL: But Kpwat had reached the shores already: he had climbed a pandanus tree and was waiting for his brothers there. No sooner had they landed on the beach than he jumped down from the tree, and destroyed his own canoe with his axe.

S.FORM: Nē sala “Gamu 'n 'ätä vinn̄i vätäl nen̄ tē hälä ma?” Gēē sa “Aa!”.
S.TRANSL: He asked them “Did you see the banana skin that was floating on the sea? — Yes,” they replied.

S.FORM: Nē sa “Na nen̄!” – “To nēk ēn row kēl make naha ma heg?”
S.TRANSL: “Well, he added, that was me! — But how did you even get here?!”

S.FORM: Nē sa “Vinlah! Gamu ok ēn äqä wutä nen̄, na nen̄! Na lē vinlah nen̄.”
S.TRANSL: “Aboard a coconut!” he replied, “You remember the one you threw away? well, that was me. I was in that coconut.”

S.FORM: We gēē tē van ajew hag [le vanō]. 🌿
S.TRANSL: So they began to walk inland to find a village. 🌿

S.FORM: Van, gēē tē n̄oo mēn too qatuu ätmät.
S.TRANSL: They found a place to sleep, at the house of a giant ogre.

S.FORM: N̄oo mun nē, ätmät nen̄ ēn 'ätä gēē, nē sa “Ha'ēh! Noknok heg, gamu ga n̄oo vaan heg lē too um̄ä heg, na na a n̄oo päh heg.”
S.TRANSL: As soon as he had seen them, the ogre had invited them to stay with him: “Alright, he said, tonight you will all sleep over here in this house of mine; as for me, I’ll sleep over there.”

S.FORM: La nē ok tē gäl woo gēē to sa nē ok a vuh gēē.
S.TRANSL: But he was really fooling them, with a plan to kill them.

S.FORM: On qēn̄, nē 'n row ma, Qat ēn [sirin̄ ēn valakärän] lē sini um̄ä, gēē pah gēē tē row ol lē valakärän nen̄ gēē tē n̄oo lolon.
S.TRANSL: And indeed, that same night he set off towards that room – but Kpwat had already flicked open the central pillar of the house, and they had all walked inside to sleep there.

S.FORM: Tan̄ro nen̄ ēn row ma on qēn̄, row ma, äm gēē, gēē gaiv. Gēē va lē valakärän. 🌿
S.TRANSL: So when the evil spirit came in during the night, he searched for them everywhere, but could not find them. They were hiding in the central pillar! 🌿

S.FORM: On matpäh nē 'n row ma, nē sa: “Ey! Tuutuak! Na 'n row ma on qēn̄, gamu gaiv, gamu have?”
S.TRANSL: The next morning, he came in and asked them: “My friends! I came here during the night, but I couldn’t find you: where were you?”

S.FORM: La too tuan Qat nen̄ nē ok ga sa, nē ok a visvis on viivirin̄ ga 'ēv'ēv m̄ērē ek.
S.TRANSL: Now one of Kpwat’s brothers was a bit stupid, and would always tell away secrets like this one.

S.FORM: Nē sa “O! Nēk ēn row ma nen̄, gamä 'n 'ēv woo lē valakärän lē sini um̄ä hegi!”
S.TRANSL: “Of course, he replied. When you came to visit us, we were all hiding in this pillar, in the middle of your house!

S.FORM: Tan̄ro sa “Ha'ēh! Ga wē!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: – Oh, really?” said the ogre. “Perfect!” 🌿

S.FORM: Gēē tē van lēh lē m̄as, lä lēh gängän ma, wälwäl gängän pah, sa: “Ha'ōh! Gamu 't n̄oo lēh!” Gēē tē n̄oo.
S.TRANSL: Then they went back to the garden, picked some food again, came back to bake it. “Alright,” he said, “It’s time you went back to sleep!” and off they went to sleep.

S.FORM: On qēn̄, nē 'n row tägäh lēh ma, sa a gän gēē, Qat ēn mäkä gēē 'n n̄oo lē gah. Gah avan um̄ä.
S.TRANSL: During the night, the ogre quickly came back again to kill them, but this time Kpwat had made them sleep in the roof.

S.FORM: Nē 'n jej gah mēn pisliman m̄ērē heg, gah tē wät gēē tē row ol lolon, gēē tē n̄oo.
S.TRANSL: He had flicked open a rafter with his fingers like this, and suddenly the post split open, allowing them to jump inside and spend the night there.

S.FORM: Tan̄ro 'n row tägäh ma, äm tägäh gēē, gēē gaiv.
S.TRANSL: As the ogre rushed in, he searched them, but to no avail.

S.FORM: On matpäh, nē 'n row ma nē sa, “Eh! Gēē wēē tuutuak! Na 'n row ma on qēn̄ sa gēj a suusuu, na 'n row tägäh ma, gamu gaiv!”
S.TRANSL: The next morning, he came back and asked “Hey, my friends! I came here during the night so we could have a chat, but when I looked for you, you were nowhere to be found!”

S.FORM: We tuan Qat nen̄ ti vis mun nē sa: “O, nēk ēn row ma nen̄, i Qat ēn petn̄äg gamä lē gah! Gamä 'n n̄oo woo lē gah.”
S.TRANSL: So Kpwat’s brother replied: “Well, when you came in, Kpwat had just hidden us in the rafters! We were just sleeping inside the roof.”

S.FORM: Tan̄ro nen̄ sa: “Ha'ēh!” Nē tē van lōk lēh. 🌿
S.TRANSL: “Oh I see!” replied the ogre, and off he went. 🌿

S.FORM: Gēē tē wälwäl. Gängän lēh, on rävräv gēn nen̄, nē sa: “Alē, gamu 't n̄oo!”
S.TRANSL: So they cooked and had dinner together once again, until night came: “Alright, time y’all went to sleep!”

S.FORM: On qēn̄ nē tē row lōk lēh ma.
S.TRANSL: But once again, during the night he hurried in.

S.FORM: Row lōk lēh ma nen̄: äm tägäh gēē, jej tägäh gah, gēē gaiv lolon.
S.TRANSL: Hurried in, searched them, flicked the rafters open and checked, but they were not inside.

S.FORM: La gēē va 'n n̄oo makē wolwol.
S.TRANSL: This time, they were sleeping in the cross beam.

S.FORM: On matpäh nē 'n row lōk lēh ma, tuan Qat nen̄ sa / nē sala: “Ēh, wēē tuutuak! Na 'n row ma on qēn̄ sa gēj ga suusuu, gamu gaiv!”
S.TRANSL: When he came back in the morning, he asked “Hey, my friends! I came here during the night so we could have a chat, but you weren’t here.”

S.FORM: We tuan Qat nen̄ sa: “Oh, nēk ēn row ma nen̄, i Qat ēn petn̄äg gamä lē wolwol maken heg, gamä 'n n̄oo maken heg.” Sa “Ha'ēh!” 🌿
S.TRANSL: One of Kpwat’s brothers replied: “That’s because Kpwat had hidden us in the cross beam up over there, we were simply sleeping inside.” – “Oh alright.” he said. 🌿

S.FORM: We talōw avan ēhē nen̄, gēē gēn tē wälwäl lēh to nen̄, Qat sa: “Wēē tuutuak, na tē mäkä kere gēj to, la gamu tē visvis jērē gēj to, noknok heg gēj ga to' lōk lēh gēn ek!”
S.TRANSL: The next day, as they were cooking together again, Kpwat said to his brothers: “Brothers, I’m thinking of a solution for us all; but if you give us away, then that will be the time for us to run away!”

S.FORM: Sa “Noknok heg, na tē petn̄äg kere gēj to, gamu tē 'en vis on gēj to; ak, ēn manreg nok. Noknok heg gēj a mulä lēh älähä?”
S.TRANSL: “I’ll try to find us a good hiding, but don’t go about revealing it! Remember that our canoe is in pieces, how would be able to return?”

S.FORM: Alē, nē sa: “Noknok heg, gēj a wälwäl, gēē 'n wälwäl hōw m̄ērē heg, naw gaiv. E! Too sē row vil naw!”
S.TRANSL: “Here’s the plan”, he added. “Right now, we are cooking without salt. Well, one of us should go find some salt water!”

S.FORM: Alē, too tuan Qat tē van.
S.TRANSL: So one of Kpwat’s brothers went off.

S.FORM: Qat vis mun nē sa “Nēk a van, qis manreg mon̄ pō nēk tē vēgēn makē ram̄os.”
S.TRANSL: Kpwat had given him instructions: “When you get there, smash your bamboo bottle, and start climbing on a Casuarina tree.”

S.FORM: Too tuan ēn van hōw, qis manreg mon pō, row vēgēn makē ram̄os, tē hag.
S.TRANSL: So his brother went down to the coast, smashed his bottle in pieces, climbed up a Casuarina tree, and waited.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n hag jērē va–van –
S.TRANSL: His brothers waited for him for a while…

S.FORM: “Eh! (i) vä nen̄ ēn van tē 'ät'ät avōh! Too tē van lēh!”
S.TRANSL: and then: “Hey! That guy went away but is not coming back! Someone else take his turn!”

S.FORM: Ēn van sēwēl hōw, qis manreg mon pō, tē row vēgēn hag makē ram̄os, tē hag.
S.TRANSL: Another one walked to the coast, smashed his bamboo, then climbed up the tree, and waited.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n mäkä va–van m̄ērē nen̄, gēē vata pah ēn van. 🌿
S.TRANSL: They did exactly like this on and on and on, until they were all gone. 🌿

S.FORM: Alē, Qat woo mētēn i / (haha tan̄ro nen̄ i Qasval) Qasval woo 'n haghag.
S.TRANSL: Finally, the only ones left were Kpwat and… Kpwasval (that was the ogre’s name).

S.FORM: Wōrō 'n hag va–van, naw tē 'ät avōh, wōrō tē räkäs.
S.TRANSL: So the two of them waited for a while, but the salt water never came; and finally they took the baking out of the oven.

S.FORM: Räkäs mongēē wälwäl nen̄, Qat gēn tē mäkä to sa nē ok a to' jen nē.
S.TRANSL: As they were taking the food out, Kpwat was already thinking of escaping.

S.FORM: Nē 'n häläqäg tägäh m̄ērē heg, Tan̄ro tē row [tuwoo] nē.
S.TRANSL: Suddenly he tried to leap out like this, but the ogre jumped in the way.

S.FORM: Nē tē wähä Tan̄ro mēn too qet ga tutun, Tan̄ro tē häläqäg kēl talvōn um, nē tē häläqäg talvōn.
S.TRANSL: So he took a piece of hot taro and threw it at the ogre’s face; but the ogre managed to jump to the other side of the ground oven, and so did Kpwat.

S.FORM: Va–van, we tē wähä kere vata nagē Tan̄ro nen̄ mēn too qet ga tutun we nē tē ginteg.
S.TRANSL: Again, he took a piece of hot taro and through it straight onto the ogre’s face – and dashed away.

S.FORM: Ginteg hōw nen̄, tuutuan pah nok makē ram̄os. 🌿
S.TRANSL: He fled all the way to the shore, where all his brothers had climbed up the Casuarina tree. 🌿

S.FORM: Nē tē row vēgēn hag, nē gēn tē luwluw gēn ek, sa: “Mok ram̄os! Na a marēs nēk a rēg! Nēk a vutgi!”
S.TRANSL: Without further ado he rushed up the tree, and exclaimed: “My tree! I want you to grow up! Be tall!”

S.FORM: We ram̄os nen̄ tē rēg, tē vutgi ajew.
S.TRANSL: The Casuarina tree suddenly grew up and up and up till it was very tall.

S.FORM: Gēē tē vēgēn suusuu. Tan̄ro tē vēgēn suusuu gēē ma.
S.TRANSL: They started climbing one after the other – but the Ogre climbed right after them!

S.FORM: Gēē 'n vēgēn vēgēn va–n, Qat sa: “Mok ram̄os! Nēk rēg, nēk vutgi lēh hag!”
S.TRANSL: They kept climbing on and on, and Kpwat said: “My tree! Grow up once more! Be taller again!”

S.FORM: Ram̄os nen̄ tē vutgi sa tē vutgi kakaran̄kē vata hag, hag nen̄ to lē pōlō.
S.TRANSL: So the tree lengthened like crazy, reaching up all the way to the clouds.

S.FORM: Gēē 'n jēn̄ hag nen̄, sa “Ha'ēh! Mok ram̄os! Nēk ēt kaōl!”
S.TRANSL: When they managed to reach the top, he exclaimed: “Alright, my tree! Now please bend down!”

S.FORM: We 'n ram̄os nen̄ tē kaōl.
S.TRANSL: And the Casuarina suddenly bent down.

S.FORM: Kaōl kaōl kaōl va–van, jēn̄ hōw lē vanō nen̄, nē tē häläqäg jen, tuutuan tē häläqäg (jen), nē tē gih lekteg uhli ram̄os nen̄.
S.TRANSL: It bent down, down, down, all the way to an island. One after the other, the brothers jumped down from the tree – while one of them was holding the tree top firmly in his hands.

S.FORM: Tan̄ro nen̄ ēn kakal ma, va rigtäg we: nē tē ukäg ram̄os, ram̄os tē 'äqä wutä i Qasval.
S.TRANSL: But the Ogre was still climbing on all fours, and getting closer and closer… At this moment they let go of the top of the tree, and suddenly the giant Kpwasval was thrown away in the air –

S.FORM: Tē 'äqä wutä Tan̄ro nen̄: sēv lōk lēh ma Lakon.
S.TRANSL: Yes, the Ogre was thrown into the air – and fell down all the way back to this land of Gaua.

S.FORM: We i Qat, mēn tuutuan, tē haghag Vanōlav. 🌿 🌿
S.TRANSL: As for Kpwat and his brothers, they went back to live on Vanua Lava. 🌿 🌿

S.FORM: Suusuu ēn pah woo to heg, Tan̄ro tē mät.
S.TRANSL: This is how the story ends, with the death of the Ogre.

S.FORM: Gēē tē hag lōk lēh lē mongēē vanō ok gēē ok ēn row jen ēhē.
S.TRANSL: They went back to live in their island again, the one they had left before.

S.FORM: Nē gēn woo, mok suusuu.
S.TRANSL: So this was the story I wanted to tell.
